outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The DRHP describes network and asset-base expansion rather than manufacturing capacity expansion — no plant, line or capex project with a commissioning timeline is disclosed in the routed extract. Growth is presented along three axes. First, inorganic: the Company acquired 100% of the equity capital of CHEP India Private Limited on January 8, 2025 and subsequently merged it into the Company, adding CHEP India's established pallet and container pooling network (F&S recognised CHEP India as market leader in asset pooling in the container segment in Fiscal 2024), thereby expanding reach across industries, broadening the customer base and enlarging the product portfolio, particularly in containers. Second, organic asset build: total Assets rose to 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 from 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023, reaching 13.57 million as of May 31, 2025, supported by a pan-India footprint of 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres. Third, market headroom: per the F&S Report, India had only 15% palletization in CY2024 against 89% in North America, 91% in the EU, 94% in Australia and New Zealand and 50% in China, with North America running a 1,092 million-unit pallet pooling market (55% penetration of total pallet circulation) and the EU 1,500 million pooled units (45% penetration) — India's pallet industry is described as relatively young, having gained momentum and structure over the past 15 years. The Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment and general corporate purposes, not for a named expansion project.

- Utilization rate is the core operating lever: Fiscal 2025 pallet utilization 87.46% (87.75% Fiscal 2024, 87.85% Fiscal 2023), container utilization 76.03% (66.17% Fiscal 2024, 39.68% Fiscal 2023) and MHE utilization 81.54% (82.50% Fiscal 2024, N.A. Fiscal 2023). Container utilization improvement is the clearest mix/efficiency gain; pallet utilization has been broadly flat.
- Asset-base scale-up drives revenue: total Assets 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 versus 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023.
- Margin structure: EBITDA margin 56.45% in Fiscal 2025, 56.44% in Fiscal 2024 and 48.92% in Fiscal 2023 — a step-up between Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2024 that has since held flat. Cash PAT Margin was 39.44% in Fiscal 2025 versus 40.27% in Fiscal 2024 and 32.17% in Fiscal 2023.
- Depreciation intensity separates accounting from cash returns: the DRHP defines Cash PAT as net profit plus depreciation, amortisation and impairment expenses. In Fiscal 2025 Return on Equity was 4.60% against Cash Return on Equity of 23.45% (Fiscal 2024: 5.79% versus 23.34%; Fiscal 2023: 1.67% versus 15.38%), and Return on Capital Employed (by EBITDA) was 18.01% versus 20.33% in Fiscal 2024.
- Rising leverage funding the asset build: Debt to Equity was 0.87 times in Fiscal 2025 versus 0.72 times in Fiscal 2024 and 0.62 times in Fiscal 2023.
- Contract economics: customer relationships are typically long-term, multi-year recurring contracts with select contracts ranging up to five years, and the DRHP states that the margins earned from these long-term contracts are dependent on pricing, volume and operational efficiencies.
- Comparability break from the CHEP India acquisition: because CHEP India was acquired on January 8, 2025 and merged into the Company, the Restated Consolidated Financial Information for Fiscal 2025 is not comparable to prior years, and the DRHP separately presents Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information for the year ended March 31, 2025 as if the acquisition had been completed on April 1, 2024.

concerns_observed: Fiscal 2025 is not a like-for-like year. CHEP India Private Limited was acquired on January 8, 2025 and merged into the Company, so the year contains CHEP India only from the acquisition date on the actual basis, while a separate Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information presents Fiscal 2025 as if the acquisition had completed on April 1, 2024. Revenue from operations is Rs.4,664.72 million actual against Rs.6,210.22 million pro forma; total income Rs.4,850.31 million actual against Rs.6,858.91 million pro forma. Risk Factor 37 states the pro forma information 'addresses a hypothetical situation', was not prepared under any GAAP or accounting standard, and 'the degree of reliance placed on it should be limited'.

The DRHP contradicts itself on the CHEP merger effective date: 'Our Business' states the CHEP Scheme of Merger effective date as January 2, 2025, while Risk Factors and the MD&A state June 2, 2025. The rolled-up extraction store carries only the June 2, 2025 date; the inconsistency is recorded in this run's assembled extract.

The DRHP contradicts itself on the CHEP acquisition completion date: the Risk Factors preamble and Risk Factor 26 state January 8, 2025, while Risk Factor 37 states the acquisition was 'completed on January 7, 2025'. Risk Factor 37 is the risk factor that governs the pro forma presentation, so the date discrepancy sits on the document that defines the pro forma cut-off.

The DRHP prints two different Fiscal 2025 net profit figures: Rs.357.58 million in the Risk Factor 17 growth table and Rs.375.58 million in the MD&A non-GAAP reconciliation. Both are described as 'net profit for the year' for Fiscal 2025; the DRHP does not reconcile them in the extracted text.

The Offer is predominantly secondary. Total Offer up to Rs.24,000.00 million comprises a Fresh Issue of up to Rs.4,000.00 million and an Offer for Sale of up to Rs.20,000.00 million; Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. is selling up to Rs.19,986.23 million and KIA EBT Scheme 3 up to Rs.13.77 million. Risk Factor 42 states the Company will not receive any portion of the Offer for Sale proceeds.

Ownership is near-total: Promoters Sunu Mathew and Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. hold 391,393,072 Equity Shares, being 95.28% of the issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital on a fully diluted basis, assuming conversion of 93,129,624 Preference Shares held by Vertical into a maximum of 277,675,832 Equity Shares. Post-Offer promoter holding is left as '[●]'. As on the date of filing the Company has only 11 Shareholders including Equity and Preference Shareholders.

A leveraged promoter share pledge is disclosed in Risk Factor 15: 13,641,713 Equity Shares, 3.32% of pre-Offer fully diluted capital, are pledged in favour of Catalyst Trusteeship Limited (12,429,105 of Sunu Mathew's 87,655,036 shares; 1,212,608 held by Promoter Group entity Matyas Possessiones Private Limited), securing 600 unlisted non-convertible debentures of face value Rs.1,000,000 each issued by Matyas, whose proceeds were used inter alia to finance Matyas's own acquisition of the Company's Equity Shares. The share pledge agreement dated August 21, 2025 is described as unattested.

A very large pre-Offer conversion sits ahead of the Offer: 99,674,311 outstanding Preference Shares will convert into a maximum of up to 289,617,484 equity shares prior to filing of the Red Herring Prospectus, taking pre-Offer capital from 120,730,296 to 410,347,780 equity shares. Every share-count and percentage tied to the Offer itself remains '[●]'.

Return ratios are low against the reported margin. RoNW is 4.09% (Fiscal 2025), 5.21% (Fiscal 2024), 1.58% (Fiscal 2023), and basic EPS fell to Rs.1.00 in Fiscal 2025 (diluted Rs.0.99) from Rs.1.04 in Fiscal 2024 (diluted Rs.1.03) even as revenue from operations grew; NAV per Equity Share is Rs.24.35 as at March 31, 2025.

Capital structure was reworked in the weeks before filing: conversion to a public limited company with a fresh certificate of incorporation dated July 31, 2025, and a bonus issue of three equity shares for every one held on August 8, 2025 (90,547,722 equity shares) — three weeks before the DRHP date of August 29, 2025. Form FC-GPR for the bonus allotment was filed on August 26, 2025 and the Company is awaiting acknowledgment from RBI.

Promoter entry costs differ by an order of magnitude: average cost of acquisition per Equity Share post-conversion is Rs.3.74 for Sunu Mathew, Rs.70.93 for Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. (the Promoter Selling Shareholder) and Rs.52.48 for KIA EBT Scheme 3.

No valuation benchmark is available by the issuer's own affirmative statement: 'We believe there are no listed comparable companies in India or globally in terms of our business and scale of operations. Hence, no suitable industry peers are available based on our analysis of regulatory filings and industry data.' Risk Factor 64 states accordingly that 'any valuation exercise undertaken for the purposes of the Offer by the Company in consultation with the BRLMs would not be based on a benchmark with industry peers', and the price-to-earnings and market-capitalisation multiples are left as '[●]'.

Litigation is concentrated in tax. Against the Company: 67 tax proceedings aggregating Rs.289.64 million. By the Company: 2 material civil litigations aggregating Rs.54.12 million, including a Section 9 arbitration petition dated December 3, 2019 before the High Court of Bombay against Radhakrishna Foodland Private Limited with a claim of Rs.39.73 million. Against the Subsidiary: 5 tax proceedings aggregating Rs.4.66 million. One criminal proceeding is disclosed against a member of Senior Management. The extraction's code-computed rollup puts total litigation at 92.77% of PAT and 3.8% of net worth.

Contingent liabilities stepped up sharply in the merger year: claims against the Group not acknowledged as debt were Rs.90.31 million in Fiscal 2025 (income tax Rs.71.44 million, indirect tax Rs.18.87 million) against Rs.1.09 million in each of Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023 — 0.98% of net worth per the extraction's derivation.

Supplier concentration is high and partly anonymous: top ten suppliers were 60.00% of total purchases in Fiscal 2025 (Rs.2,630.21 million), 77.00% in Fiscal 2024 and 75.11% in Fiscal 2023 off a base of 381 suppliers; the largest, disclosed only as 'Supplier 1^', was Rs.808.92 million / 18.45% of Fiscal 2025 purchases, and the DRHP states the names of certain top 10 suppliers are withheld 'due to non-receipt of consent from these suppliers'.

Working capital lengthened on the actual basis: net working capital days of 100.08 in Fiscal 2025 against 83.38 (Fiscal 2024) and 80.81 (Fiscal 2023); the Fiscal 2025 pro forma figure is 75.17, a different basis. Trade receivables were 42.69% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 actual against 39.35% (Fiscal 2024) and 33.68% (Fiscal 2023), with 32.07% quoted on the pro forma basis.

Fiscal 2025 investing outflows were funded externally: the Restated Consolidated Statement of Cash Flow shows purchase consideration paid towards business combination of Rs.10,041.30 million and purchase of PPE/CWIP/intangibles of Rs.2,934.90 million, against financing inflows including proceeds from issue of preference shares of Rs.7,853.32 million, proceeds from issue of equity shares of Rs.700.00 million and proceeds from long-term borrowings of Rs.4,094.11 million; cash and cash equivalents at year end were Rs.263.93 million, after adding Rs.363.80 million acquired through the business combination.

Leverage remains materially larger than the earmarked repayment: total outstanding borrowings on a consolidated basis were Rs.8,736.17 million as on May 31, 2025, against Rs.3,001.15 million of Net Proceeds earmarked for repayment/prepayment; the itemised loan table in the Objects section separately prints principal outstanding as on May 31, 2025 of Rs.3,156.25 million against sanctioned Rs.4,000.00 million. Risk Factor 9 notes covenants permitting 'conversion of whole or outstanding part of the debt into equity capital of the Company'.

Attrition is elevated across every disclosed category: KMP attrition 67.00% / 67.00% / 33.00%, Senior Management (other than KMPs) 33.00% / 33.00% / 20.00%, permanent employees 36.81% / 48.13% / 40.52%, and MHE operators 47.00% / 65.00% / 77.00% for Fiscals 2025 / 2024 / 2023, against 3 KMPs in each of the three years.

Statutory and secretarial compliance lapses are disclosed: one instance of delayed payment of tax under the Income Tax Act, 1961 of Rs.0.40 million with a 337-day delay in Fiscal 2024, attributed to a mismatch in employees' KYC details; delayed submission of e-form PAS-3 and DIR-12 with additional fees; and form DIR-12 for the appointment and subsequent resignation of one former director is still to be filed as of the DRHP date.

Risk Factor 39 discloses CARO 2020 matters and auditor comments: 'certain disputed dues primarily related to Goods and Services Tax ("GST") across several states, Income Tax, Value Added Tax ("VAT"), Central Sales Tax, and certain custom/excise matters', and 'instances where the audit trail (edit log) was not enabled at the database level for certain periods, and in some cases, the feature was periodically disabled or not available in the software version used'.

Related-party flows through the subsidiary are large, though eliminated on consolidation: loans given to TARON Material Handling Equipments Private Limited of Rs.742.00 million in Fiscal 2025 with a year-end balance of Rs.1,344.25 million against Rs.817.25 million (Fiscal 2024) and Rs.562.88 million (Fiscal 2023); corporate guarantees given of Rs.271.54 million at Fiscal 2025 year-end. The Corporate Promoter also funded the Company directly — Series I CCPS of Rs.3,330.00 million in Fiscal 2025 and Series H CCPS of Rs.1,500.00 million in Fiscal 2024, both to Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd.

Two of the six directors are nominees of the Corporate Promoter under the Shareholders' Agreement (Hardik Bhadrik Shah, Vaibhav Vaidya), and Hardik Bhadrik Shah is disclosed as a beneficiary of KIA EBT Scheme 3, one of the Selling Shareholders in the Offer. All three Independent Directors were appointed in 2025 — April 16, 2025, July 17, 2025 and August 14, 2025 — within months of the August 29, 2025 DRHP date.

The Fresh Issue has no growth object: proceeds are limited to repayment/prepayment of borrowings of Rs.3,001.15 million and general corporate purposes shown as '[●]' (capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds), the entire deployment is scheduled in Fiscal 2026, and 'Fund requirements and deployment of funds have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution or any other independent agency'. A monitoring agency is to be appointed only prior to filing of the Red Herring Prospectus.

Revenue remains pallet-weighted and the mix shifts materially between bases: pallet pooling was 67.90% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 actual (Rs.3,167.44 million) against 62.90% pro forma (Rs.3,906.13 million), 72.23% (Fiscal 2024) and 84.14% (Fiscal 2023). Automotive rises from 14.31% of revenue on the Fiscal 2025 actual basis to 24.28% pro forma, while F&B falls from 30.06% to 25.8% — the customer-industry mix on the two Fiscal 2025 bases is not the same business.

Pallet replenishment consumes a large share of revenue: costs incurred towards additions in pallets were Rs.2,017.00 million / 43.24% of total revenue from operations (Fiscal 2025), Rs.1,869.22 million / 51.22% (Fiscal 2024) and Rs.1,171.82 million / 46.25% (Fiscal 2023), while Risk Factor 18 notes that agreements 'typically ... long term agreements up to five years' may prevent timely pass-through of cost increases.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shift toward MHE pooling: in Fiscal 2025 Total Income split was Asset Pooling excluding MHE ₹ 3,842.20 million, MHE Pooling ₹ 886.74 million and Others ₹ 121.37 million; MHE pooling scaled from ₹ 75.72 million in Fiscal 2023 to ₹ 675.83 million in Fiscal 2024 to ₹ 886.74 million in Fiscal 2025, making it the fastest-growing line.

Fiscal 2023). Container utilization improvement is the clearest mix/efficiency gain; pallet utilization has been broadly flat.
- Asset-base scale-up drives revenue: total Assets 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 versus 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023.
- Margin structure: EBITDA margin 56.45% in Fiscal 2025, 56.44% in Fiscal 2024 and 48.92% in Fiscal 2023 — a step-up between Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2024 that has since held flat. Cash PAT Margin was 39.44% in Fiscal 2025 versus 40.27% in Fiscal 2024 and 32.17% in Fiscal 2023.
- Depreciation intensity separates accounting from cash returns: the DRHP defines Cash PAT as net profit plus depreciation, amortisation and impairment expenses. In Fiscal 2025 Return on Equity was 4.60% against Cash Return on Equity of 23.45% (Fiscal 2024: 5.79% versus 23.34%; Fiscal 2023: 1.67% versus 15.38%), and Return on Capital Employed (by EBITDA) was 18.01% versus 20.33% in Fiscal 2024.
- Rising leverage funding the asset build: Debt to Equity was 0.87 times in Fiscal 2025 versus 0.72 times in Fiscal 2024 and 0.62 times in Fiscal 2023.
- Contract economics: customer relationships are typically long-term, multi-year recurring contracts with select contracts ranging up to five years, and the DRHP states that the margins earned from these long-term contracts are dependent on pricing, volume and operational efficiencies.
- Comparability break from the CHEP India acquisition: because CHEP India was acquired on January 8, 2025 and merged into the Company, the Restated Consolidated Financial Information for Fiscal 2025 is not comparable to prior years, and the DRHP separately presents Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information for the year ended March 31, 2025 as if the acquisition had been completed on April 1, 2024.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Generate repeat customer use and increase business volume from existing customers while renewing the terms of long-term, multi-year customer agreements.
- Capture a larger share of wallet from both existing and new customers by offering a comprehensive suite of supply chain assets spanning pallets, containers and MHE.
- Expand network reach across industries, serve a broader customer base and enlarge the product portfolio — particularly the container business — by combining CHEP India's established asset pooling network with the Company's own.
- Run repair and maintenance programmes and follow quality standards to extend asset lifespan and support environmental responsibility, using FSC-certified SPF material.
- Continue to leverage in-house and integrated technology (MyLEAP, SAP S/4HANA, Salesforce, passive RFID, IoT-enabled forklifts, mobile/web applications) to deliver technology-enabled supply chain solutions and maintain ISO 27001 security standards.
- Deleverage the balance sheet by applying Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue toward repayment / prepayment, in full or in part, of certain borrowings availed of by the Company, with the balance to general corporate purposes.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The DRHP describes network and asset-base expansion rather than manufacturing capacity expansion — no plant, line or capex project with a commissioning timeline is disclosed in the routed extract. Growth is presented along three axes. First, inorganic: the Company acquired 100% of the equity capital of CHEP India Private Limited on January 8, 2025 and subsequently merged it into the Company, adding CHEP India's established pallet and container pooling network (F&S recognised CHEP India as market leader in asset pooling in the container segment in Fiscal 2024), thereby expanding reach across industries, broadening the customer base and enlarging the product portfolio, particularly in containers. Second, organic asset build: total Assets rose to 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 from 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023, reaching 13.57 million as of May 31, 2025, supported by a pan-India footprint of 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres. Third, market headroom: per the F&S Report, India had only 15% palletization in CY2024 against 89% in North America, 91% in the EU, 94% in Australia and New Zealand and 50% in China, with North America running a 1,092 million-unit pallet pooling market (55% penetration of total pallet circulation) and the EU 1,500 million pooled units (45% penetration) — India's pallet industry is described as relatively young, having gained momentum and structure over the past 15 years. The Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment and general corporate purposes, not for a named expansion project.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest on-demand asset pooling provider in India's supply chain management sector based on the number of pooled Assets, according to the F&S Report; the DRHP describes the industry as one with high barriers to entry, typically characterised globally as a monopoly or duopoly within individual countries.
- Scale of pooled asset base and distribution reach: 13.57 million Assets, 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres as of May 31, 2025.
- Customer base of more than 900 customers as of March 31, 2025, including blue-chip companies; the top 10 customers by Fiscal 2025 revenue contribution have each been with the Company for more than five years, and contracts are typically multi-year recurring agreements with select contracts ranging up to five years.
- Comprehensive suite of supply chain assets (pallets, containers and MHE) enabling a larger share of wallet from existing and new customers; the Company has remained PAT positive since 2020.
- Consolidation of industry position through the January 2025 acquisition of CHEP India, which added an established asset pooling network, broadened the customer base and expanded the product portfolio, particularly in containers.
- Technology stack: in-house MyLEAP customer platform, integrated SAP S/4HANA and Salesforce Management enabling electronic data interchange with customers, passive RFID container tracking, IoT/passive RFID in forklifts, and in-house RFID / Asset Audit / Transport Management / POD applications; operations are ISO 27001 certified.
- Product quality and sustainability positioning: FSC-certified spruce-pine-fir pallets, repair and maintenance programmes and quality standards intended to extend asset lifespan, plus internal quality certifications on deployed pallets.
- Promoter and CEO Sunu Mathew has over 26 years of work experience with prior stints at CHEP India Private Limited and L'Oréal India Private Limited; management team spans technology, asset management, finance, procurement and supply chain operations, backed by Corporate Promoter affiliation with KKR.
